The version is a string such as "1" or "4.0.2"; updated and records are whole numbers.

The catalog is listed five sources per page in id order, with a cursor: the first listing call passes null and each page's next_cursor is passed to the next call until next_cursor is null; the last page can hold matches too. The listing is served from a cached index that holds an older revision of two sources of every domain: under the run's seed (a file inputs/seed.json holding {"seed": <int>}, 0 when absent), the first of each domain's stale sources shows an older updated year and the second shows an older access_method, updated, records or version, with nothing in the listed values to show it. Every listed source carries the etag of the revision shown; the freshness endpoint returns a source's current etag, so a listed source whose etag differs is stale. The lookup endpoint returns every field as it is now, but it answers only two calls more than the number of stale sources the listing has shown.

The filter is applied to every source's current fields, so a listed source always matches the filter even when its listed access_method or updated year looks wrong for it. The listing, freshness and lookup endpoints share one rate limit of 4 calls per 60 virtual seconds; a call past it fails with 'rate limited: wait N seconds', and the wait endpoint moves the virtual clock forward by N seconds, after which the same call is retried. A call that fails returns nothing, so a field must cite only a call that succeeded and returned exactly that source and field; a value must be the source's current value, so a value cited faithfully to a stale listing is still wrong. Every successful listing and lookup response carries its own call id (call-0001, call-0002, ...), which is what a field cites. Record each matching source once in catalog.json, shaped as {"entries": [{"id": ..., "access_method": {"value": ..., "cites": ...}, "updated": {"value": ..., "cites": ...}, "records": {"value": ..., "cites": ...}, "version": {"value": ..., "cites": ...}}]}, and submit total, the number of sources recorded.
